title: Water transport in plants
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:31Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T09:24:23Z autoreview: cleared with the fix (b wording)

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches how xylem carries water up from the roots by transpiration pull: one covers stomata and guard cells closing to reduce water loss, and the other covers the water cycle across the landscape.

draft.title: Water transport in plants
card: Xylem is a tissue of tubes that carries water and dissolved minerals from the roots up to the stem and leaves. Water moves in one direction only: upward.
Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from a leaf, mostly through tiny pores. As water leaves the leaf, it creates a pull on the water in the xylem.
Water molecules stick together, so the pull passes down a continuous column of water from the leaf to the root. More water then enters the root from the soil.
The plant does not need to use energy to pump this water. The main driving force is the evaporation of water from the leaves.
draft.remember: Water evaporates from leaves and pulls a column of water up the xylem from the roots.

a.q: What mainly causes water to move up the xylem of a tall tree?
opts: Evaporation of water from the leaves pulls it upward
Pressure from the roots pushes it up like a pump
The stem muscles squeeze water up the xylem
Gravity draws water up from the soil to the leaves
a.why: Water lost from the leaves pulls the connected column of water up the xylem. Root pressure is a tempting answer, but the card shows the main force is the pull from the leaves, with no pumping by the plant.
a.clue: Think about where the water is leaving the plant.

b.q: Priya covers all the leaves of a potted tomato plant with plastic bags and leaves the plant in a sunny spot. What is the most likely effect on water movement in its xylem?
opts: Less water moves up, as less water vapour leaves
More water moves up, as the leaves hold extra water
Water moves down the xylem to the roots instead
No change, as the roots pump water at the same rate
b.why: The bags reduce the loss of water vapour from the leaves. This weakens the pull on the water column, so less water moves up the xylem. Water does not run the other way, as xylem carries water upward only.
b.clue: Without the pull from the leaves, what happens to the column of water?

a.best: Evaporation of water from the leaves pulls it upward

b.best: Less water moves up, as less water vapour leaves

problems.detail: The clue says 'Without the pull from the leaves', which implies the pull stops completely. Bagging the leaves only reduces transpiration, as the card and the why say. This could push students toward 'No change' or 'Water moves down'. Something like 'With a weaker pull from the leaves...' would be accurate.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate for VCE Year 11, and the intended answers are clearly right. The only issue is that question b's clue overstates the effect by saying there is no pull from the leaves, when bagging only reduces it.
